newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress names Kesri as parliamentary leader.
newsitem.headline: India Congress names Kesri as parliamentary leader.

text.p: Lawmakers from India's Congress party chose Sitaram Kesri on Friday as leader of the party's parliamentary party to replace former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
"The consensus is in favour of Sitaram Kesri," former finance minister Manmohan Singh told a meeting of the Congress Parliamentary Party.

Kesri, who became Congress party president in September when Rao stepped down under pressure, beat back a youthful challenge from former cabinet minister Rajesh Pilot, who had won backing from Rao loyalists.
Rao, who was prime minister from 1991 until last May and spearheaded a drive to open up India's economy, quit under pressure as Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader last month.

He had retained considerable influence as Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition depends on Congress's backing to survive against the Hindu nationalist opposition in the lower house of parliament.

On Thurday, Pilot, 51, had said he wanted a secret ballot to choose a new parliamentary leader. But former cabinet minister G. Venkatswamy said Kesri had been unanimously elected by the members of the CPP, which has a total strength of 225.
